question: A curve that joins all points representing bundles which are considered indifferent by the consumer is called a/an ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**indifference curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **indifference curve** represents a series of combinations of two goods that provide equal utility or satisfaction to a consumer.
 
• It is a graphical representation in microeconomics used to illustrate consumer preferences.
 
• The curve is typically downward sloping, indicating that as the quantity of one good increases, the quantity of the other good must decrease to maintain the same level of satisfaction.
 
• Indifference curves do not intersect, as each curve represents a different level of utility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Consumer Curve:**

 
 
• There is no specific economic concept termed as a "consumer curve". This term is incorrect in this context.
 
 
 
• **Marginal Curve:**
 
 
• A marginal curve typically represents the marginal utility or marginal cost. Marginal utility refers to the additional satisfaction gained from consuming one more unit of a good.
 
 
 
• **Indifference Curve:**
 
 
• An indifference curve shows combinations of goods that provide the same level of utility to the consumer, implying that the consumer is indifferent between these combinations.
 
• It is used in consumer theory to analyze consumer preferences and the trade-offs they are willing to make between different goods.
 
 
 
• **Utility Curve:**
 
 
• A utility curve represents the relationship between the quantity of goods consumed and the total utility derived from consuming those goods.
 
• It is typically used to illustrate the concept of total utility rather than showing combinations of goods that provide equal satisfaction.
